skill.name: mobile-debugging
skill.description: Guide Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through React Native and Expo debugging workflows for Metro, native modules, device logs, builds, performance, and crashes.
skill.summary: Troubleshoot React Native and Expo apps with targeted debugging commands, logs, checklists, and performance checks.
skill.author: BabakBar

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate React Native and Expo debugging guide, not a prompt injection or malware attempt. Several static findings are false positives from Markdown fences and documentation links, but the guide does include destructive local reset and process-kill commands that require user confirmation and care.

remediation.issue: Destructive cleanup commands are presented as direct fixes.
remediation.suggestion: Add confirmation steps before rm -rf, simulator erase, adb restart, and process-kill commands, and explain what state each command deletes.

remediation.issue: Global package installation is recommended for React DevTools.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer project-local or npx-based execution where possible to reduce global environment changes.

remediation.issue: Device and application logs can contain sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users to avoid sharing unredacted logs and to remove tokens, API URLs, and personal data before posting output.

content.value_statement: Mobile app failures often span Metro, native build tools, devices, and JavaScript runtime behavior. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured debugging path for React Native and Expo projects.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses Metro bundler cache and module resolution problems.
Guides iOS pod resets, Android Gradle cleanup, and Expo prebuild troubleshooting.
Collects and interprets Metro, iOS, Android, and adb log output.
Suggests React Native performance checks for slow renders and memory leaks.
Provides a reproducible debugging checklist for crashes, build errors, and platform-specific failures.
limitations: Requires access to the local mobile project and installed native tooling.
Some suggested commands can delete cache, simulator data, or generated native files.
Does not replace Xcode, Android Studio, or physical device testing.
Cannot guarantee fixes for third-party native module defects.

use_cases.title: Resolve Metro startup failures
use_cases.description: Use structured cache, dependency, and port checks when Metro fails to start or cannot resolve modules.

use_cases.title: Investigate native build errors
use_cases.description: Walk through iOS pod, Android Gradle, and Expo prebuild checks when native builds fail after dependency changes.

use_cases.title: Triage crashes and performance regressions
use_cases.description: Collect logs, compare platforms, inspect render time, and check cleanup patterns after an app crash or freeze.

prompt_templates.title: Start a basic mobile debug session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to help me debug this React Native issue. Start by asking for the error message, platform, recent changes, and reproduction steps.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Metro bundler problem
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to diagnose why Metro cannot resolve modules in my project. Check safe steps first before suggesting destructive cache cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze native build failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to investigate this iOS or Android build failure. Review dependency changes, native logs, and platform-specific cleanup options.

prompt_templates.title: Run a full crash and performance review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the mobile-debugging skill to build a React Native crash investigation plan. Include log sources, reproduction checks, platform comparison, memory cleanup, and render performance analysis.

output_examples.input: Metro starts, then says it cannot resolve a module after I renamed a file.
output_examples.output: A short triage plan that checks import casing, file existence, cache state, and recent dependency changes before recommending a cache reset.

output_examples.input: Android builds fail after adding a native package.
output_examples.output: A platform-focused checklist covering package compatibility, Gradle cleanup, adb logs, and native exception details.

output_examples.input: The app freezes after opening a screen several times.
output_examples.output: A debugging sequence that checks reproduction steps, device logs, slow renders, subscriptions, timers, and missing cleanup functions.

best_practices: Capture the full error message and stack trace before running cleanup commands.
Confirm destructive commands with the user and explain what data they remove.
Compare iOS, Android, simulator, emulator, and physical device behavior when possible.
anti_patterns: Deleting caches or generated files before preserving the original error output.
Sharing raw device logs without redacting tokens, URLs, and personal data.
Assuming a JavaScript fix when the failure is isolated to one native platform.

faq.question: Does this skill run mobile debugging commands automatically?
faq.answer: It provides command guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Destructive commands should still require user review and confirmation.

faq.question: Can it debug both React Native CLI and Expo projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers Metro, Expo commands, React Native logs, native build cleanup, and platform-specific tools.

faq.question: What tools should be installed first?
faq.answer: A working Node environment, project dependencies, and the required iOS or Android tooling for the target platform are needed.

faq.question: Will it fix production crash reports?
faq.answer: It can guide crash triage and log analysis, but production symbolication and crash service access may still be required.

faq.question: Is it safe to use the cleanup commands?
faq.answer: Many cleanup commands are common but can delete local caches, simulator data, or generated files. Review each command before running it.

faq.question: Can this skill help with performance issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for slow renders, missing cleanup in effects, memory leaks, and platform-specific logs.
